record.original_question: If sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal or symplectic involution on a central simple algebra A over F, must sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to every odd-degree field extension of F?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1. Suppose sigma is an anisotropic orthogonal or symplectic involution on a central simple algebra A over a field F. Does sigma remain anisotropic after scalar extension to any odd-degree field extension of F?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F$ be a field and let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central simple algebra over $F$. Recall that an $F$-linear involution $\sigma\colon A\to A$ (i.e., an anti-automorphism of order $2$ fixing $F$) is said to be of orthogonal or symplectic type according to the conjugacy class of its restriction over an algebraic closure. The involution $\sigma$ is called isotropic if there exists a nonzero element $a\in A$ with $\sigma(a)a=0$ that lies in a nonzero right ideal $I\subseteq A$ satisfying $\sigma(I)\cdot I=0$; otherwise $\sigma$ is called anisotropic. For a field extension $L/F$, let $\sigma_L$ denote the involution on $A_L=A\otimes_F L$ obtained by extending scalars.

Question: Suppose $\sigma$ is an anisotropic involution of orthogonal or symplectic type on $A$. Must $\sigma_L$ be anisotropic for every finite field extension $L/F$ of odd degree?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (a Springer-type question for involutions) is known in several cases but remains open in general. Positive answers have been established for hermitian forms over quaternion algebras with involutions of the first kind (including in characteristic two), and equivalences with other major conjectures (e.g., preservation of anisotropy under generic splitting fields, due to Karpenko, Tignol, and Karpenko–Zhykhovich) have been proved. No general resolution for arbitrary central simple algebras with orthogonal or symplectic involutions appears in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Involutions, odd-degree extensions and generic splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses preservation of anisotropy of involutions under odd-degree extensions and links it to generic splitting via results of Karpenko, Tignol, Karpenko–Zhykhovich.
status_evidence.claim: The Springer-type question for involutions has been linked to generic splitting and resolved in some cases but not in general.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonal involutions and totally singular quadratic forms in characteristic two
status_evidence.snippet: An anisotropic hermitian form over a quaternion algebra with involution of the first kind in characteristic two remains anisotropic over all odd degree extensions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem has positive answers for quaternion algebras with first-kind involutions.

status_evidence.title: On anisotropy of orthogonal involutions (Karpenko)
status_evidence.snippet: Karpenko's work on anisotropy of orthogonal involutions and equivalence with conjectures on generic splitting.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results equate this question to other major open conjectures.
